objects.description: Core HTTP message parser state machine object from Joyent http_parser. Holds parser configuration, running state, and read-only results for the current message. Users initialize with http_parser_init(), drive it with http_parser_execute(), and consult fields and callbacks. It is not thread-safe and is intended to be stack- or heap-allocated by the caller; no destructor is required.
Callback vtable used by http_parser to notify the application during parsing. Must be zero-initialized or initialized via http_parser_settings_init(), and populated with function pointers as needed.
Enumeration of all supported HTTP request methods, e.g., HTTP_GET, HTTP_POST, including WebDAV, UPnP, CalDAV, and LINK/UNLINK. Values are stable indices used by the parser.
Specifies parser operating mode: request-only, response-only, or both (for HTTP/1.x tunneling/proxy scenarios). Used when initializing http_parser.

objects.definition:
enum flags
  { F_CHUNKED               = 1 << 0
  , F_CONNECTION_KEEP_ALIVE = 1 << 1
  , F_CONNECTION_CLOSE      = 1 << 2
  , F_CONNECTION_UPGRADE    = 1 << 3
  , F_TRAILING              = 1 << 4
  , F_UPGRADE               = 1 << 5
  , F_SKIPBODY              = 1 << 6
  , F_CONTENTLENGTH         = 1 << 7
  };
objects.description: Bitmask flags used internally in http_parser.flags to track message properties (chunked transfer, connection semantics, trailing headers, etc.). Intended for semi-internal use; values are public constants.
Enumeration of parser error codes (HPE_*). Used to report parsing and callback errors via http_parser.http_errno and related helper APIs.

objects.definition: typedef int (*http_data_cb) (http_parser*, const char *at, size_t length);
objects.description: Function pointer type for data callbacks (e.g., URL, status, header field/value, body). Return non-zero to signal error/stop parsing.
Function pointer type for non-data parser callbacks (message/chunk boundaries, headers complete). Return non-zero to signal error or special conditions as documented.

Result container for http_parser_parse_url(). field_set is a bitmask of which components are present; field_data provides offsets/lengths into the provided URL buffer; port is parsed/converted if present.

  , UF_HOST             = 1

objects.description: Indices for components of a parsed URL used with http_parser_url.field_data[]. UF_MAX is the count of addressable fields.

functions.name: http_parser_version
functions.description: Returns the library version encoded into a single unsigned long. Bits 16–23 contain the major version, bits 8–15 the minor, and bits 0–7 the patch. Useful for runtime version checks.

functions.name: http_parser_init
functions.description: Initializes an http_parser instance for parsing HTTP messages of the specified type (request, response, or both). Sets internal state to defaults prior to use with http_parser_execute.
requirements: parser must be a valid, writable pointer to an http_parser struct
type must be one of enum http_parser_type values (HTTP_REQUEST, HTTP_RESPONSE, HTTP_BOTH)
Call before the first http_parser_execute on this parser instance

functions.name: http_parser_settings_init
functions.description: Zero-initializes an http_parser_settings struct so all callbacks are disabled by default. Callers can then assign only the callbacks they need before executing the parser.
requirements: settings must be a valid, writable pointer to an http_parser_settings struct
Call before passing settings to http_parser_execute

functions.name: http_parser_execute
functions.signature: size_t http_parser_execute(http_parser *parser, const http_parser_settings *settings, const char *data, size_t len);
functions.description: Parses up to len bytes from data using the provided callbacks in settings, advancing the parser state and invoking callbacks as input is consumed. Returns the number of bytes successfully parsed. On error, sets parser->http_errno and stops. If an Upgrade header is encountered causing the parser to exit, parser->upgrade will be set and should be checked after return.
requirements: parser must be a valid http_parser previously initialized with http_parser_init
settings must be a valid pointer to an http_parser_settings (callbacks may be NULL to disable)
data must point to a buffer of at least len bytes
Callbacks must return 0 on success; non-zero return indicates error and halts parsing
on_headers_complete may return 1 to indicate no body is expected (e.g., response to HEAD)
on_headers_complete may return 2 to indicate no body and no further responses are expected on the connection (e.g., CONNECT)
Caller should check parser->http_errno on non-OK return conditions and may inspect parser->upgrade after return

functions.name: http_should_keep_alive
functions.description: Determines whether the connection should be kept alive after the current message. Intended to be called from on_headers_complete or on_message_complete callbacks.
requirements: parser must be a valid pointer to an http_parser whose state reflects a parsed message up to headers_complete or message_complete
If this returns 0, the caller should close the connection or send a "Connection: close" header as appropriate

functions.name: http_method_str
functions.description: Returns the string representation of the given HTTP method enum value (e.g., "GET", "POST").
requirements: m should be a valid enumerator from enum http_method

functions.name: http_errno_name
functions.description: Returns a short string name for the specified parser error code (e.g., "HPE_INVALID_METHOD").
requirements: err should be a valid enumerator from enum http_errno

functions.name: http_errno_description
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description string for the specified parser error code.
requirements: err should be a valid enumerator from enum http_errno

functions.name: http_parser_url_init
functions.description: Initializes all members of http_parser_url to zero before use with http_parser_parse_url.
requirements: u must be a valid, writable pointer to a struct http_parser_url

functions.name: http_parser_parse_url
functions.signature: int http_parser_parse_url(const char *buf, size_t buflen, int is_connect, struct http_parser_url *u);
functions.description: Parses the URL in buf and populates u with offsets/lengths for each URL component. Returns 0 on success and nonzero on failure. If parsing succeeds, u->field_set contains a bitmask indicating which UF_* fields are present, and u->port contains the numeric port if present. The is_connect flag indicates parsing of a CONNECT target form.
requirements: buf must point to a buffer containing the URL of length buflen
u must be a valid, writable pointer to a struct http_parser_url (typically zero-initialized via http_parser_url_init)
Callers should only read u->field_data[UF_*] entries when the corresponding bit is set in u->field_set
Offsets and lengths in u->field_data index into the original buf
Function returns nonzero on failure; caller must check the return value
is_connect is a nonzero/zero flag indicating CONNECT-style parsing semantics

functions.name: http_parser_pause
functions.description: Pauses or unpauses the parser. When paused (paused != 0), parsing halts; pass paused == 0 to resume before the next http_parser_execute call.
requirements: parser must be a valid pointer to an http_parser
paused nonzero pauses the parser; zero unpauses it before subsequent http_parser_execute calls

functions.name: http_body_is_final
functions.description: Indicates whether the current body chunk is the final one. Useful when handling chunked transfers to know if more body data will follow.
requirements: parser must be a valid pointer to an http_parser reflecting the current parsing state (typically called during/after on_body or related callbacks)

data_types.description: A byte buffer containing an HTTP/1.x request or response. May include start-line (request line or status line), headers terminated by CRLF, optional message body possibly using Content-Length or chunked transfer encoding. Supports upgrade headers and various methods/status lines. Arbitrary binary bytes may appear in the body.

A single URL/URI in text form as defined for HTTP parsing. May include scheme, host, optional port, path, query, and fragment components. Input is a contiguous character buffer of length buflen; offsets in the parsed result reference this buffer.

Some common header names and value generators COMMON_HEADERS = [ b"Host", b"User-Agent", b"Accept", b"Accept-Encoding", b"Accept-Language", b"Connection", b"Content-Type", b"Content-Length", b"Transfer-Encoding", b"Upgrade", b"Expect", b"TE", b"Trailer", b"Proxy-Connection", b"Range", b"If-Modified-Since", b"If-None-Match", b"Authorization", b"Cookie", b"Set-Cookie", b"Date", b"Server", b"Cache-Control", b"Pragma" ] UA_STRINGS = [ b"curl/8.4.0", b"Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 Chrome/118 Safari/537.36", b"Wget/1.21.4", b"python-requests/2.31.0" ] CONTENT_TYPES = [ b"text/plain", b"application/json", b"application/octet-stream", b"application/x-www-form-urlencoded", b"text/html", b"multipart/form-data; boundary=boundary42" ] ENCODINGS = [b"gzip", b"deflate", b"br", b"identity"] UPGRADES = [b"websocket", b"h2c", b"TLS/1.0, HTTP/1.1", b"h2c, h2"] PATHS = [ b"/", b"/index.html", b"/api/v1/resource", b"/submit", b"/search", b"/chunked", b"/upload", b"/range/bytes", b"/redirect", b"/long/path/with/components" ] QUERIES = [b"q=test", b"a=1&b=two", b"empty=", b"arr=1&arr=2", b"token=abc123"] HOSTS = [b"example.com", b"localhost", b"www.test.local", b"[::1]", b"127.0.0.1"] COOKIES = [b"sid=abc; theme=light", b"a=1; b=2", b"csrftoken=xyz"] # Helpers def _rand_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes: return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n)) def _maybe(r: random.Random, p: float) -> bool: return r.random() < p def _random_token(r: random.Random, min_len=3, max_len=12) -> bytes: alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnoqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789-_.~" ln = r.randint(min_len, max_len) return bytes(alphabet[r.randrange(len(alphabet))] for _ in range(ln)) def _build_request(r: random.Random) -> Tuple[bytes, bool]: # returns (message, has_body) method = r.choice(METHODS) # Build target: absolute path, authority form for CONNECT, or absolute URL use_absolute = _maybe(r, 0.2) if method == b"CONNECT": target = r.choice(HOSTS) + b":" + str(r.randint(1, 65535)).encode() else: if use_absolute: scheme = r.choice([b"http", b"https"]) \ + b"://" + r.choice(HOSTS) path = r.choice(PATHS) if _maybe(r, 0.5): path += b"?" + r.choice(QUERIES) target = scheme + path else: path = r.choice(PATHS) if _maybe(r, 0.5): path += b"?" + r.choice(QUERIES) target = path ver = r.choice(HTTP_VERS) start = method + b" " + target + b" " + ver + _crlf() headers: List[Tuple[bytes, bytes]] = [] # Mandatory-ish headers if ver == b"HTTP/1.1" and method != b"CONNECT": headers.append((b"Host", r.choice(HOSTS))) # Connection semantics conn = None if _maybe(r, 0.5): conn = r.choice([b"keep-alive", b"close", b"upgrade"]) headers.append((b"Connection", conn)) # Upgrade flow if conn == b"upgrade" and _maybe(r, 0.8): up = r.choice(UPGRADES) headers.append((b"Upgrade", up)) # TE and Trailer if _maybe(r, 0.3): headers.append((b"TE", b"trailers" if _maybe(r, 0.5) else b"chunked")) if _maybe(r, 0.2): headers.append((b"Trailer", b"Expires, X-Final")) # User-Agent and Accept if _maybe(r, 0.7): headers.append((b"User-Agent", r.choice(UA_STRINGS))) if _maybe(r, 0.6): headers.append((b"Accept", b"*/*")) if _maybe(r, 0.4): headers.append((b"Accept-Encoding", b", ".join(r.sample(ENCODINGS, k=r.randint(1, min(3, len(ENCODINGS))))))) # Cookies if _maybe(r, 0.4): headers.append((b"Cookie", r.choice(COOKIES))) has_body = method in (b"POST", b"PUT", b"PATCH") or _maybe(r, 0.2) # Body strategy: content-length or chunked body = b"" use_chunked = False if has_body and method != b"CONNECT": if _maybe(r, 0.5): # content-length body ctype = r.choice(CONTENT_TYPES) headers.append((b"Content-Type", ctype)) # Build meaningful bodies for some types if ctype == b"application/json": # small JSON key = _random_token(r, 3, 8) val = _random_token(r, 3, 8) body = b'{"' + key + b'":"' + val + b'"}' elif ctype.startswith(b"multipart/form-data"): boundary = ctype.split(b"boundary=")[-1] part1 = b"--" + boundary + _crlf() + \ b"Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"field\"" + _crlf() + _crlf() + \ b"value" + _crlf() part2 = b"--" + boundary + _crlf() + \ b"Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"file\"; filename=\"a.bin\"" + _crlf() + \ b"Content-Type: application/octet-stream" + _crlf() + _crlf() + \ _rand_bytes(r, r.randint(0, 64)) + _crlf() end = b"--" + boundary + b"--" + _crlf() body = part1 + part2 + end elif ctype == b"application/x-www-form-urlencoded": body = b"a=1&b=two&token=" + _random_token(r, 4, 12) elif ctype == b"text/plain": body = b"Hello, world!\n" * r.randint(0, 4) else: body = _rand_bytes(r, r.randint(0, 128)) headers.append((b"Content-Length", str(len(body)).encode())) else: # chunked transfer use_chunked = True headers.append((b"Transfer-Encoding", b"chunked")) ctype = r.choice(CONTENT_TYPES) headers.append((b"Content-Type", ctype)) else: # Methods with no body often include Content-Length: 0 if method in (b"GET", b"HEAD", b"DELETE", b"OPTIONS") and _maybe(r, 0.5): headers.append((b"Content-Length", b"0")) # Expect header if _maybe(r, 0.2) and method in (b"POST", b"PUT", b"PATCH"): headers.append((b"Expect", b"100-continue")) # Range if _maybe(r, 0.2): start_b = r.randint(0, 50) end_b = start_b + r.randint(0, 200) headers.append((b"Range", f"bytes={start_b}-{end_b}".encode())) # Compose headers header_lines = b"".join(h + b": " + v + _crlf() for h, v in headers) msg = start + header_lines + _crlf() if use_chunked: # Build valid chunked body with optional extensions and trailers chunks: List[bytes] = [] num_chunks = r.randint(1, 5) for _ in range(num_chunks): data_len = r.randint(0, 128) data = _rand_bytes(r, data_len) ext = b"" if not _maybe(r, 0.3) else b";foo=bar" chunks.append(hex(len(data))[2:].encode() + ext + _crlf() + data + _crlf()) final = b"0" + (_crlf() if not _maybe(r, 0.4) else b";fin=1" + _crlf()) trailers = b"" if _maybe(r, 0.5): trailers_list = [(b"X-Final", b"1"), (b"Expires", b"0")] trailers = b"".join(k + b": " + v + _crlf() for k, v in trailers_list) msg += b"".join(chunks) + final + trailers + _crlf() else: msg += body return msg, has_body def _build_response(r: random.Random) -> bytes: ver = r.choice(HTTP_VERS) code, reason = r.choice(STATUSES) start = ver + b" " + str(code).encode() + b" " + reason + _crlf() headers: List[Tuple[bytes, bytes]] = [] # " elif ctype == b"text/plain": body = reason + b"\n" else: body = _rand_bytes(r, r.randint(0, 128)) headers.append((b"Content-Length", str(len(body)).encode())) else: use_chunked = True headers.append((b"Transfer-Encoding", b"chunked")) headers.append((b"Content-Type", r.choice(CONTENT_TYPES))) else: # Explicit content-length 0 for clarity sometimes if _maybe(r, 0.7): headers.append((b"Content-Length", b"0")) # Accept-Ranges, ETag, Cache-Control variety if _maybe(r, 0.3): headers.append((b"Accept-Ranges", b"bytes")) if _maybe(r, 0.3): headers.append((b"ETag", b'"' + _random_token(r, 6, 10) + b'"')) if _maybe(r, 0.3): headers.append((b"Cache-Control", b"max-age=" + str(r.randint(0, 3600)).encode())) header_lines = b"".join(h + b": " + v + _crlf() for h, v in headers) msg = start + header_lines + _crlf() if use_chunked: chunks: List[bytes] = [] for _ in range(r.randint(1, 4)): d = _rand_bytes(r, r.randint(0, 96)) chunks.append(hex(len(d))[2:].encode() + _crlf() + d + _crlf()) msg += b"".join(chunks) + b"0" + _crlf() + _crlf() else: msg += body return msg def _maybe_pipeline(r: random.Random, first: bytes, is_request: bool) -> bytes: # Optionally append another message to exercise persistent connections/pipelining if not _maybe(r, 0.3): return first second = _build_request(r)[0] if is_request else _build_response(r) combined = first + second # ensure size cap return combined[:4096] def generate(seed: int) -> bytes: r = random.Random(seed) # Choose to emit request, response, or mixed both depending on parser mode used by fuzz stubs choice = r.random() if choice < 0.45: req, _ = _build_request(r) return _maybe_pipeline(r, req, True) elif choice < 0.9: resp = _build_response(r) return _maybe_pipeline(r, resp, False) else: # both: request then response to exercise HTTP_BOTH behavior req, _ = _build_request(r) resp = _build_response(r) data = req + resp return data[:4096]
